title: The Sunday Papers
description: Sundays are for realising that after playing The Blood of Dawnwalker, you've developed a craving for blackcurrant juice. There's none in the cupboard, so you venture out to get some, floating across the rooftops as a trail of mist as you go. You arrive at the supermarket, fangs bared and claws out. You parry and dodge attackers armed with trollies as you fight your way up the aisles. There it is. The sweet crimson nectar. You reach out to grab a bottle. A hand reaches out through the display and grips your wrist. Read more

title: The weird, wonderful world of Miles Buckle, Instagram's parallel universe of video games
description: Going through Miles Buckle's Instagram feed is like stumbling into a parallel universe where cinema's greats – Lynch, Hitchcock, Fellini, Kubrick – are reimagined in the familiar but distinctly different visual language of video games. The " here's Johnny " scene from The Shining, where Jack Nicholson terrorises Shelley Duvall, recreated in the stilted comedic style of The Sims 2. The opening sequence of Twin Peaks told through the landscapes of SimCity 2000 – one of several "orthographic experiments" that Buckle has done using the most iconic Maxis game of my childhood. A low-poly Peter Finch doing the Oscar-winning "I'm a human being, god dammit!" monologue from Sidney Lumet's classic Network. Perfect fever dreams that can't and won't exist outside of these short clips. Read more

title: WoW Forever Will Add All-New Content To Classic Azeroth This November
description: World of Warcraft Forever is Blizzard's next iteration on WoW Classic, one that will add new content in the form of zones, quests, dungeons, raids, and even a new playable race while keeping the old-school MMORPG's world and gameplay intact. Revealed during BlizzCon 2026's opening ceremony, WoW Forever is Blizzard's attempt to give WoW Classic fans the "forever" game they've wanted for years. However, instead of the MMO progressing to the game's subsequent expansions and their new areas, as Classic has in the past, WoW Forever will instead keep the focus on WoW's original two continents, Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Within that Classic backdrop will be up to 1,000 new quests, Blizzard said, as well as revamped zones, and three entirely new zones that fill out areas present on the map in vanilla WoW but were never accessible to players. There will be nine new dungeons to explore, two raids, and an additional PvP battleground. A new playable race is also part of the package: the Skyborne elves. One of the new playable zones will be their starting area, Blizzard said. In addition to all-new content, Blizzard will be revamping classes with new talents and skills, as well as allowing for new class and race combinations. An option to toggle HD visuals and old-school graphics will also be included. Blizzard will continue to update WoW Forever with new content, but won't raise the level cap past 60. Unlike modern WoW, WoW Forever won't be focused on the endgame experience. Blizzard said many of the new dungeons and quests will be for characters under level 60. That aligns with what Blizzard said were its core principles in how it approached development of WoW Forever--that it should be about the journey, not the destination; the world itself is a character; and the game's social aspects should be a focus. For those who want to continue experiencing the original version of Azeroth, the normal version of WoW Classic will still be playable. Players won't have to wait long…

title: Warcraft Getting Its First New RTS Campaign In Two Decades–And It’s Playable Today
description: A new Warcraft 3 campaign exploring the origins of the Forsaken and the formation of the Undercity will be live later today, Blizzard announced as part of its BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony announcements. Titled Forsaken Kingdom, the DLC campaign will put a spotlight on the last days of Lordaeron after it fell to Arthas and how it became the home of the Forsaken many players are familiar with in World of Warcraft. The campaign will be available in Warcraft 3: Reforged, Blizzard's once-maligned remaster of 2003's RTS classic. While the new campaign costs money, the 3.0 update for Warcraft 3: Reforged is free and also releases today. The update adds new visual improvements and quality-of-life features. This is just the latest update to Warcraft 3: Reforged that looks to salvage its poor reputation. In 2024, Blizzard released a 2.0 update as part of the franchise's 30th anniversary that sought to address many of the common complaints players have had with the remaster since its 2020 launch. Reports from the time indicated Warcraft 3: Reforged was the victim of budget cuts and rocky development, and even saw Blizzard expand its refund policy in the wake of its release. Forsaken Kingdom will be the first new Warcraft RTS content since the release of the original Warcraft 3's Frozen Throne expansion in 2003. Earlier this year, Blizzard made it so players could access the classic version of Warcraft 3 through Battle.net without the need to also launch Warcraft 3: Reforged.

title: WoW: The Last Titan Cinematic Ups The Stakes, But First, Xal’atath
description: As is BlizzCon tradition, a new World of Warcraft cinematic premiered during the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony, setting the stage for the MMORPG's next expansion, The Last Titan. In a departure for BlizzCon, that glimpse was just about all fans learned about the new expansion, with Blizzard instead looking to put the focus more on the final content patch of the game's current Midnight expansion. That update, titled Eclipse, will consist of a climactic showdown with the franchise's current main villain, Xal'atath. An in-game cinematic shown during the ceremony revealed Xal'atath's true objective, to merge with Azeroth's worldsoul and become unstoppable. Blizzard additionally teased a new standalone game mode, and yet another expansion Remix experience, will also be coming to Midnight before the expansion's end. As for The Last Titan's setting, it takes players back to Northrend, the continent previously seen in 2008's Wrath of the Lich King expansion. Much like how Blizzard revamped Silvermoon City and the Blood Elf lands of Quel'thalas in Midnight to great results, Northrend will be completely rebuilt from the ground up. Blizzard said more details about The Last Titan will be shared next year. The Last Titan was first announced at BlizzCon 2023, when Blizzard made the unprecedented move of announcing an entire trilogy of expansions all at once. Collectively, Blizzard called the three expansions The Worldsoul Saga, with a goal of bringing together many of WoW's disparate storylines from over the last 20 years into one fitting conclusion. As the end of the trilogy, The Last Titan has a lot of expectations to live up to that the main storyline of WoW's two previous expansions, The War Within and Midnight, haven't exactly met. Regardless, it will still be exciting to see how Blizzard ties two decades' worth of story involving the Void, the Titans, and Azeroth herself together into one cohesive package.

title: Hearthstone’s First New Class In 4 Years And A More Story-Driven Journal Are On The Way
description: New class additions to Hearthstone don't come often, but the next one has been announced during BlizzCon 2026's Opening Ceremony: The Monk is coming to the card game, leaving just the Evoker as the lone class to be left out. The Monk's upcoming addition was one of several major pieces of news for Hearthstone revealed. A new expansion called Reign of the Black Empire that is set 10,000 years in the past will focus on the Black Empire and a struggle between the Old Gods and the Titans. If that excites the lore enjoyer in you, you'll also be happy to hear that the Journal is being transformed into The Journey. This is meant to give a more narrative-driven wrapper to the game, as it'll seek to tie the story together between expansions, modes, and limited-time events. The Journey will grow as you play through Reign of the Black Empire, tying together quests, achievements, and more elements of the game. As far as the Monk goes, we don't know much in terms of how they'll play. We only got a short teaser for the new class, which marks the first such addition since the Death Knight arrived in 2022. The game originally launched with nine characters before later adding Demon Hunter and then Death Knight. The Monk will arrive in March 2027, with more details coming next year. Other new features coming to Hearthstone include a new keyword, Assemble, which lets you effectively merge two minions into one, which sounds similar to Magnetize; you can pick specific text from their descriptions to create new combos. A new minion type, Aberrations, was also revealed, with their deaths feeding the gods in some way. Aberrations will be specific to Battlegrounds, which is also getting a 2v2 main ranked mode. Reign of the Black Empire releases on October 20.

description: That dastardly devil is at it again.

title: Diablo 5 Is Coming In 2029, Will Actually Star Diablo
description: Diablo 5 is coming in Spring 2029, and it will take players to a world where Diablo himself reigns supreme. Announced via a short teaser during the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony, Blizzard revealed it's already at work on the next installment of the series. Set 100 years after the defeat of Mephisto in Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred, Diablo 5 will see the Lord of Terror return. However, instead of stopping him from destroying all of Sanctuary, he will actually have already won. Blizzard teased Diablo 5's story will revolve around what heroes have to become in a post-apocalyptic world that is already destroyed. More details will be shared about the game's lore, classes, and gameplay features, during a Diablo 5 panel as part of this weekend's convention. Should Diablo 5 actually release in 2029, it will be the shortest gap between Diablo games in the franchise's history. There was a 12-year wait for Diablo 3 after Diablo 2, and another 11 years between Diablo 3 and 4. Diablo 5, in comparison, is slated to come just six years after Diablo 4--still a long time, but much shorter given the franchise's track record. Blizzard has been on record saying it wants to create new Diablo games faster. In an interview earlier this year, Blizzard said that "over the next 30 years, maybe we get some out faster."

title: Diablo 4’s Next Class Is What You Expect But Isn’t Coming With A Full Expansion
description: Diablo 4's next class is Amazon, Blizzard announced during the BlizzCon opening ceremony, but it won't be coming as part of a new expansion. Instead, Blizzard will sell the Amazon as a separate DLC class pack in the first half of next year. The addition of the Amazon isn't exactly a surprise. First, it's an iconic class from Diablo 2, so it's a bit of a no-brainer there. Alongside the nostalgia factor, Diablo 4's latest expansion, Lord of Hatred, also took players to the literal home of the Amazons, Skovos. They featured heavily in the expansion's story but were not a playable class, with the expansion instead adding the Paladin and Warlock to Diablo 4's class roster. While the Amazon isn't coming until 2027, Diablo 4's next season, Hell's Legacy, is coming much sooner. The season kicks off next week on September 15 and will celebrate the franchise's 30th anniversary and feature the return of enemies, locations, and items from previous Diablo games. That will include the return of Deckard Cain, who will take players on a journey to confront Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto, meaning the Lord of Terror himself will finally make an appearance in Diablo 4. Though it leaked ahead of time, Diablo 4 is officially coming to the Switch 2 as well, with a Lord of Hatred collection that includes both of the game's expansions.

title: Overwatch Is Reworking Two Of Its Most Criticized Characters
description: After years of complaints, Overwatch is finally reworking two of its veteran heroes. Announced during BlizzCon 2026's opening ceremony, both Roadhog and Sombra will be receiving major reworks, with Sombra pivoting to being a support hero and Roadhog undergoing changes to make him more of a team player. Shortly after the reveal, Overwatch shared an updated look at both character's Hero kits. Below is a comprehensive overview of their changes: Sombra Of the two, Sombra is receiving the most significant redesign, pivoting from a Damage hero to Support. Whereas she used to be most effective at fast-paced, ambush-style combat, she will now be far more useful in team settings. Her Hack ability has been replaced with Hotfix, which allows her to freely hack health packs and enemy deployables as well as heal allies. Cyberspace replaces Virus, and sees Sombra launch a projectile that heals allies and weakens enemies. With the exception of CTRL ALT ESC, all of Sombra's Perks have been adjusted, and she now boasts Support passives. Roadhog By comparison Roadhog's changes are far less dramatic, with the most notable being the removal of Scrap Gun's Alt Fire. In lieu of this skill, Roadhog has been given Trash Compactor--an ability that allows Roadhog to absorb enemy projectiles and turn them into an explosive ball of scrap. This makes him far more effective as an actual Tank, granting him what seems like a fairly effective barrier that will hopefully deter players from abandoning their team in search of smaller firefights. In addition to these changes, Blizzard has announced Overwatch's 54th character, Doctrine, is coming October 5.

title: Overwatch’s Newest Blood-Sucking Character Pushes The Game Even Further Into The Fantasy Genre
description: Since its inception, Overwatch has positioned itself as an optimistic, science-fiction-driven world. Although some characters have introduced an element of the fantastical--the addition of the magical Wuxing University being the most notable tonal shift--the team behind the hero shooter has always prioritized scientific explanations for its heroes incredible abilities. Its newest character, however, seems to venture further into fantasy than ever before. Revealed during BlizzCon 2026's opening ceremony, Doctrine is the next support hero coming to Overwatch. Oh and fun fact, he's a vampire--or vampire-inspired, at the very least. With a sceptre that heals and speeds up teammates yet dishes out major damage to enemies, Doctrine is an extremely powerful hero with a high mechanical floor. Interested in putting your skills to the test and giving him a whirl? You're in luck, as Doctrine's limited-time hero trial has officially kicked off and will run until September 14. In addition to his sceptre, Doctrine can also unleash a swarm of bat drones, infuse allies, and "manipulate life force." Blizzard has described the hero as the "ultimate vampire fantasy." Below is a more thorough look at his Hero kit: While Doctrine (real name Tamuka Yeukai) hails from Zimbabwe, he is accompanied by the Escort map Watchpoint: Grimsvotn, which depicts the Icelandic prison he is seen escaping in his debut cinematic. Doctrine joins Overwatch on the side of Talon, his trailer revealing him to be a close friend of Doomfist. This relationship also expresses itself mechanically, as the Overwatch team stated his kit complements Doomfist's extremely well. In other Overwatch news, the team shared that two of its most criticized legacy characters, Sombra and Roadhog, are undergoing major changes.

title: StarCraft Is Officially Back, But It’s Taking A Much Different Form
description: Following numerous rumors dating back many months, it's official: StarCraft is returning with a new game, but that game won't be in the traditional real-time-strategy genre the franchise is known for. Instead, the new StarCraft game is described as an open-world shooter. The news was revealed as part of BlizzCon's opening ceremony. However, that's essentially all we know, as the new game-referred to only as StarCraft--won't be released until 2030. As such, there were no further details shared about how it will play or anything else. After Blizzard's Dan Hay said, "It's about damn time" that we returned to the interstellar war of StarCraft, we did see a cinematic trailer. Dominion forces are shown being pumped up after being trained as elite warriors. They're then sent onto the battlefield against a massive wave of Zerg forces. When it does arrive, this will mark the first original game in the StarCraft franchise since the StarCraft II trilogy wrapped up with Legacy of the Void in 2015. The original game did receive a remaster, StarCraft Remastered, in 2017, but Blizzard's focus has otherwise shifted to its other franchises over the last decade. While a StarCraft shooter had been rumored for some time, the reveal is still sure to come as a contentious piece of news for fans starved for a traditional StarCraft game. (The audible reaction from the crowd when "open-world shooter" was said was not necessarily one of elation.) This isn't the first attempt to spin off the series into something else, as StarCraft Ghost was meant to be a stealth-action entry, but it was ultimately canceled prior to release. A recent report indicated that Nexon is seeking the StarCraft license in order to make a new game--possibly StarCraft III--so there may still be some hope for another StarCraft RTS. Teases for a StarCraft revival began earlier this month, after the game's official website started to "glitch" and fans discovered hidden text logs. Each one appeared to be a secret…

title: Diablo Animated Series Coming To Netflix, Other Blizzard Franchises Teased
description: Well, that was unexpected. As part of the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony, studio president Johanna Faries announced that Blizzard is partnering with Netflix on an animated Diablo series. The announcement was made as Faries emphasized the studio is called Blizzard Entertainment, meaning it doesn't intend to limit itself to games. Overwatch and Warcraft were also specifically mentioned after the Diablo series' announcement, though Faries did not say if anything is official or concrete at this stage. Blizzard is no stranger to non-interactive adaptations of its games, of course, with the Warcraft movie releasing about a decade ago. That movie didn't exactly light the world on fire, critically or commercially, but an animated series or two may better fit Blizzard's IP. No timeline was given for when we could see the Diablo animated series, but it was just one of several big announcements the company made during its opening ceremony. The biggest on the Diablo front included the debut of the Amazon in Diablo 4 and the reveal of Diablo 5.

title: Heroes of the Storm gets first new hero after supposed death and 6 year wait
For The First Time In 6 Years, Blizzard Is Bringing A New Character To Heroes Of The Storm
description: Heroes of the Storm, Blizzard's MOBA mashup of its various franchises, has largely remained unchanged since its developers moved onto other priorities back in 2022. But as WoW's long-running storylines are moving toward a conclusion that involves Xal'atath, that character is set to be added to HotS, and she arrives quite soon. Blizzard revealed the new addition as part of the BlizzCon Opening Ceremony. Xal'atath will join the Public Test Realm beginning this Monday, September 14, with a full release set for September 28. This will mark the first new character since Warcraft's Hogger was added in 2020. While Xal'atath might turn out to be a one-off addition to the game, it was teased that another character could be added in the future. Given balance updates and a skin have represented the bulk of what's changed since Hogger's launch, it's welcome to see anything of substance arrive for HotS.

title: BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony: All The Biggest Announcements And Games
description: BlizzCon is a big deal if you're a fan of all things Blizzard, and the weekend event kicked off with a traditional opening ceremony full of announcements and reveals for the company's biggest games--and a few surprises! The biggest of these included the announcement that StarCraft will return in 2030, but this time, Blizzard is switching up genres as the sci-fi game goes from real-time strategy to open-world shooter. Diablo 5 was also announced, and World of Warcraft fans were spoiled with several reveals. In case you missed it, you can catch all the trailers and news below. Heroes of the Storm Heroes of the Storm is adding a new hero to its roster for the first time in six years, as Xal'atath is coming to the Nexus. You can try her out starting Monday on the PTR. For The First Time In 6 Years, Blizzard Is Bringing A New Character To Heroes Of The Storm A Diablo animated series is in development at Netflix The next announcement was about a Diablo animated series in development. Blizzard president Johanna Faries announced that it's being produced by Netflix. "Diablo, I promise, is just the beginning," Faries teased. "To our Overwatch community, to our Warcraft community, and who knows, perhaps even some of our other universes." Diablo Animated Series Coming To Netflix, Other Blizzard Franchises Teased StarCraft returns in 2030 Ubisoft veteran Dan Hay was on stage to announce a brand-new StarCraft, which he described as an open-world shooter. The cinematic trailer showed off some gung-ho Dominion recruits training to be the best in the galaxy, but a few hours later, the remains of these fresh-faced soldiers were being scraped out of their warsuits. StarCraft Is Officially Back, But It’s Taking A Much Different Form Overwatch Overwatch director Aaron Keller was next on stage, dressed in an incredible jacket themed around the game. title: What Is A FOB In Wardogs And Why Do You Need One?
description: Since the monumental launch of Wardogs, which saw almost 350,000 people logging in to play when it released into early access, there's been some confusion around certain items and processes despite the in-game tutorial. While the tutorial explains how to get a FOB--or Forward Operating Base--it's easy to forget that when you're feeling the pressure of combat. FOBs are also far more useful than the tutorial explains, and they're vital to ensuring your team maintains control of the zone, increasing your points. We've got all you need to know about FOBs, how to get them, what they are, and how you can use them to your team's advantage. First of all, a FOB is a Forward Operating Base, and can be placed anywhere in the playable map apart from in your spawn base. You also won't be able to place a FOB if an opposition team's FOB is in the nearby area. Within the FOB's area of effect, your team can build structures but enemy teams cannot. To build one, you'll have to buy one from an equipment vendor. It takes up a 2x3 slot in your backpack, and won't fit in the free backpack, so you'll have to buy the upgraded version. To place the FOB after you've bought it and moved it to wherever you want to build it, press the hotkey you assigned it to, and then hold left click to place it. Each new FOB includes a free small and medium hammer and some healing bandages and other supplies. The reason building a FOB is so vital is it creates a small zone where your team can build walls, defenses, weapons, structures, and other buildings. Usually, these are placed at the towers, although they can be placed anywhere within the zone of control. The FOB allows your team to build a fortified area that can be used offensively or defensively. For example, if you've got four mortars within a base, and that base is heavily fortified, it'll be difficult for the enemy team to infiltrate the base and prevent your mortar operators from damaging them, their vehicles, buildings, and equipment. On the…
